title: Social & Psychological Portrayal: Ábrázol, bemutat, tükröz

sections.title: Describing 19th-Century European Novels
sections.content: When discussing 19th-century Romantic and Realist novels, Hungarian uses transitive verbs of portrayal (*ábrázol* 'depicts', *bemutat* 'presents', *tükröz* 'reflects') governing the accusative (`-t`), paired with instrumental phrases (`-val/-vel`) indicating artistic method (*lélektani mélységgel*, *társadalmi érzékenységgel*).

sections.title: Official Exam Roster: 19th-Century European Novels (Explained)
rows: Russian Romantic novel in verse: Eugene Onegin rejects Tatyana's sincere love out of bored cynicism, embodying the 'superfluous man' (felesleges ember) who realizes his mistake too late.
Charles Dickens: Twist Olivér, Karácsonyi ének
English Realist novels: Oliver Twist exposes the harsh life of London orphans and workhouses; A Christmas Carol shows the miser Scrooge's moral awakening to empathy.
Lev Tolsztoj: Háború és béke, Anna Karenina
Russian Realist masterworks: War and Peace paints a monumental panorama of Russian families during Napoleon's 1812 invasion; Anna Karenina examines tragic passion and social judgment.
Fjodor Mihajlovics Dosztojevszkij: Bűn és bűnhődés
Psychological novel: impoverished student Raskolnikov commits murder under a false theory of superiority, only to discover that human conscience and redemption cannot be escaped.

items.spanish: Puskin Anyegin című verses regénye a kiábrándult „felesleges ember” típusát ábrázolja.
items.english: Pushkin's verse novel Eugene Onegin depicts the archetype of the disillusioned 'superfluous man'.

items.spanish: Charles Dickens nagy együttérzéssel mutatja be az ipari forradalom árnyoldalait és a szegény sorsú gyermekek életét.
items.english: Charles Dickens presents the dark side of the Industrial Revolution and the lives of impoverished children with great compassion.

items.spanish: Tolsztoj Háború és béke című nagyregénye a napóleoni háborúk korát tükrözi.
items.english: Tolstoy's great novel War and Peace reflects the era of the Napoleonic wars.
